sentences.text: The Air Force message on Telegram read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference.

sentences.text: There is no radiation threat!
sentences.article_title: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation threat, Air Force says

sentences.text: Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel." The Ukrainian Central Intelligence Agency said on Telegram that there had been a failure in the app, and urged people to use other sources of information to clarify the situation regarding the threat of air strikes.

sentences.text: Don't go outside." A series of all clear messages were then delivered to users' phones, which were connected to each of the previous alerts, individually declaring each threat clear.

sentences.text: Airbnb host Lisa says her Welsh holiday let was left 'a complete mess' by a group of guests When Lisa Clewes returned to her Welsh holiday let after a group of guests checked out, she was horrified by the mess.

sentences.text: Emergency responders at the scene of a strike on Ukraine's Vinnytsia region A rare humanitarian ceasefire in Ukraine's front-line Kherson region that allowed civilians to evacuate the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has ended.

sentences.text: The localised ceasefire was due to end at 22:59 Ukrainian time (21:00 GMT) on Sunday.

sentences.text: While the truce had held since it was implemented last week, fighting had continued elsewhere.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: On Sunday evening, Ukraine's air alert system was apparently hacked, the country's air force said, warning of radiation over Kyiv - a reference to a possible nuclear attack.

sentences.text: The Air Force message read: "The Air Alarm application has probably been subjected to hostile interference.

sentences.text: Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had struck energy infrastructure in four regions overnight on Saturday, leaving hundreds of thousands of homes without power.

sentences.text: Some connections were restored on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: Another overnight strike killed two people, including a 13-year-old girl, in the Vinnytsia region, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.

sentences.text: Meanwhile, Ukraine hit a major missile fuel producer in Russia's Rostov region, which caused a fire and damaged four production facilities, Zelensky said.

sentences.text: In Ukraine, repair works to restore power continued throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: Most customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region had their connections restored by early evening, but more than 60,000 were still without power, the governor said.

sentences.text: Because of regular attacks on energy infrastructure, emergency power cuts have been introduced across the country.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: Even in the capital Kyiv, electricity is cut off for most of the day, and water supplies are also disrupted.

sentences.text: Zelensky said in a social media post that the intensity of Russian strikes has been "extremely high" over the past week, adding that Russia was "trying to take maximum advantage of the shortage of ballistic missile interceptors".

sentences.text: He added that "every day" Ukraine communicated its need for Patriot missiles - the only effective weapon for downing Russia's deadly ballistic missiles - to the US, Europe and other partners.

sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: It was originally confined to the city of Oleshky, which has been occupied by Russia since the first days of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and was expanded across the wider region of Kherson.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: Oleshky had been trapped on one side by the Dnipro river and the other by Russian forces, with routes out mined and subject to drone attack.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: Residents trapped there were suffering severe shortages of food, water and electricity, with many resorting to cooking garden weeds to survive.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: The truce allowed for Oleskhy residents to evacuate if they wanted, and there were emotional scenes on Saturday of reunions between loved ones who hadn't seen eachother for years.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: There are Ukrainian military positions just 5km (3.1 miles) from Oleshky, but evacuees had to travel through Russian-occupied territory to southern Russia, where they flew to Belarus, before finally being driven across Ukraine's northern border.
sentences.article_title: Russian strikes cut power to thousands in Ukraine as Kherson ceasefire ends

sentences.text: The oldest evacuee was 94 years old, while the youngest was one, according to Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman.

sentences.text: A video circulating on social media appears to show a Merseyside Police officer hitting a youth in Speke, in Liverpool A police force has said it is reviewing a video which shows one of its officers punching a boy.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: The footage circulated on social media shows a Merseyside Police officer punching what appears to be teenage boy three times while holding a pair of metal handcuffs in the hand he is striking him with.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: The force said officers had been responding on Friday to reports of about 20 youths in the Alder Wood Avenue area of Speke, Liverpool, blocking roads with wheelie bins and "aiming fireworks at anyone who tried to remove them".
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: "We would like to stress that a short clip doesn't always show the full context," a Merseyside Police spokesman said.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: The footage being circulated on social media - which has been viewed more than 40,000 times - begins moments before the officer strikes the boy.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: It does not show anything that happened in the run-up to the incident.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: Merseyside Police said youths had reportedly "smashed windows of nearby flats, tried to start fires and threatened members of the public".
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: In the video, the boy is punched in the stomach, chest and throat before he is handcuffed and dragged off the ground by the officer, then led to a police van.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: Another teenager can be seen being pulled from the ground as he is arrested.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: After a complaint was made on Saturday, the force said its professional standards team would look into the incident.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: "While we look to establish the full circumstances of what happened, we would urge people not to speculate and avoid sharing rumours or misinformation," the force said in a statement published on its website.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: The incident happened the night before Halloween, on what in Liverpool has become known as "Mischief Night".
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: "We are determined to protect our communities from the sort of appalling behaviour that we historically see at this time of year.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: "We have a contempt for criminality and a commitment to cracking down on people committing serious offences in Merseyside," a force spokesman added.
sentences.article_title: Police probe video of officer hitting youth with handcuffs

sentences.text: Some protesters were carried away by police after refusing to walk when arrested More than 300 people have been arrested during a protest supporting the banned Palestine Action group outside the US embassy, police have said.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Hundreds of people gathered at Nine Elms in London on Saturday, with many holding signs reading phrases such as: "I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action." The Metropolitan Police said on Sunday that 325 arrests were made.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: The force added on social media that 320 of them were for "expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act".
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: At least 4,000 arrests have been made in relation to the group, which was proscribed in July 2025.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: The UK Supreme Court is due to review Palestine Action's ban under terrorism legislation , after the group's co-founder was granted permission to appeal it.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: The Home Office has said that it will robustly defend against the appeal.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Officers on Saturday made arrests into the evening, taking people to police vans for transfer, to the applause of many protesters, some of whom chanted: "Free, free Palestine." In some instances, officers had to carry demonstrators who refused to walk.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Retired lawyer Charles Allison - who was taken by police in the afternoon  - had travelled from Cumbria to participate.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: He said he feared for people's civil liberties, which he said were "being devalued and watered down".
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: "I hope the Supreme Court justices - they won't necessarily be influenced by it [the protest] - but I hope that they will take a long-term view of what is happening in this country and decide that the proscription was unlawful, as I believe it was," the 75-year-old said.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: David Bolden, another protester awaiting arrest called the ban an "absurd law".
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Defend Our Juries, which has been co-ordinating a series of protests over the ban, said the number of people detained this weekend took the total over 4,000 arrests since the group was proscribed, calling it "truly dystopian".
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: According to Home Office figures seen by the BBC, 3,630 arrests were made in the year ending June 2026.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Along with the 134 people arrested outside Westminster Magistrates Court earlier this year and those on Saturday brings the total up to 4,089.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: The BBC has contacted the Met to confirm any figures it might hold.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Amnesty International UK has criticised the arrests and called for the government to drop the proscription of Palestine Action.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Defend Our Juries called the arrests "unjust" and an assault on free speech.
sentences.article_title: More than 300 arrests at Palestine Action support protest outside US embassy

sentences.text: Cate McHugh was crowned winner of The Voice UK on Saturday night A singer who began her career as a teenager busking on the streets of Cardiff has been crowned winner of The Voice UK.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: Cate McHugh, from Llantwit Major in the Vale of Glamorgan, appeared stunned when she heard her name announced on the ITV show, telling viewers "I did it" when asked how she was feeling.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: The performer, who has a degenerative sight condition which has left her registered blind, was given a congratulatory hug by her coach Sir Tom Jones on his final appearance on the show after previously announcing he had been "fired" .
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: Speaking after the show, McHugh, 31, said: "I won The Voice!
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: I'm entirely gobsmacked and absolutely haven't fully processed this information just yet." Footage shared by McHugh on social media showed her laughing and smiling with family and friends screaming in delight as they celebrated her victory at a watch party in Cardiff.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: McHugh's prizes include a £50,000 cash prize and a recording contract, with her first ever single, a cover of The Beatles classic Blackbird, now released.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: Posting on social media, she said: "From the bottom of my heart I want to say THANK YOU for following my journey, and joining my world!
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: This is where it's going to REALLY get fun!" sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: Her rendition of Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars song Die With A Smile prompted Sir Tom to hit the button to turn his chair around after hearing her.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: McHugh said she began singing "before I was talking" and started singing lessons aged six, turning professional when she was about 15.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: At 22 she was diagnosed with degenerative sight condition Stargardt disease during her second year at music school and is registered blind.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: As it affects the centre of her vision, it meant the singer was not sure if anyone had turned around at her audition until she heard Sir Tom's voice, she added.

sentences.text: "I just waited because I didn't know that anything had happened and then Tom Jones started talking," McHugh said.
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: She said her "fantastic mother" has the same condition and has been an inspiration to her over the years, "working around anything that might be affecting her physically or mentally".
sentences.article_title: Cate McHugh wins The Voice UK after being mentored by Sir Tom Jones

sentences.text: McHugh said when she phoned her parents to tell them she was on Team Tom "there was this massive roar".

sentences.text: The Green Party is at a "crossroads" and needs to focus on its "core values", a former party co-leader has told the BBC, weeks after members adopted a motion declaring Zionism a form of racism.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Adrian Ramsay suggested the Greens need their policies to appeal to a majority of British voters if they want to bring the "environmental changes that we need" and advised against taking an approach that risks being "quite divisive".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski responded by saying there was "no environmental justice without social, racial and economic justice".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: The motion, which Polanski did not take part in or vote upon, defined Zionism as an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state" that had led to the "disenfranchisement and destruction" of Palestinians.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: I would not have voted for Zionism motion, Polanski says It backed the creation of a "single democratic Palestinian state in all of historic Palestine", which includes modern-day Israel.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Members of the Green Party of England and Wales adopted the policy motion last month.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: It led to a backlash from some Jewish groups, as well as criticism from senior Green figures, including Ramsay and other Green MPs.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Israel's foreign ministry said it had banned Polanski , who is Jewish, from entering the country.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: The Equality and Human Rights Commission also wrote to the Green Party asking for more information about the motion after concerns were raised by dozens of Labour and Lib Dem MPs and Jewish campaigners.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Labour later said it would end power-sharing agreements with the Greens on local councils, unless its councillors disowned the policy.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Speaking to Newscast , Ramsay replied "no, it's not" when asked if he thought Zionism is racist before adding he agreed with Polanski and others in believing that what is happening in Gaza is "appalling".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: The MP for Waveney Valley, who joined the party in 1998, said he does think Israel has a right to exist, something Polanski has stopped short of saying.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: The Fight For The Future Of The Green Party Ramsay also said he has made it clear he is "deeply uncomfortable" with the motion adopted and suggested there is an "opportunity to take some action in relation to the motion in the run-up" to the party's spring conference next year.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: He said the question now is how Polanski and the party as a whole responds to the motion.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Ramsay said: "I think there's a real crossroads point for the party at the moment.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: He added: "What I want to see is the party really focus back in on our core aims as a party and our core values." Ramsay said this includes ensuring the party is "consensus-building in how we approach our politics" and that "we engage the grassroots of our membership".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: He added the party needs to be "very externally focused, because we're only going to be able to bring the environmental changes that we need to have to safeguard our society for now and for the future if the majority of the British public come behind that".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Ramsay served as co-leader of the Greens from 2021 to 2025 alongside Carla Denyer, who is also now an MP.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: He unsuccessfully stood on a joint ticket with fellow MP Ellie Chowns in 2025, with the pair losing to Polanski in the leadership contest .
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Polanski, who missed the conference vote to unsuccessfully campaign for election in a Westminster by-election, previously said he wants to see the "imperfect" motion amended in future.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: However, he said the "substantial part of the motion", that "the displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people is clearly underpinned by a racist ideology" was "obvious".
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Under Green Party rules, motions supported by members become official party policy, but will not necessarily be included in the party's manifesto at the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Green Party at 'crossroads' after Zionism vote, says former co-leader

sentences.text: Police Scotland received 144 fireworks-related calls on Halloween Police Scotland received 144 fireworks-related calls on Saturday night - down on 160 on 31 October last year.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Fireworks were thrown at people, buildings and vehicles in some parts of Scotland on Halloween.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Officers said in general there was "outstanding behaviour and co-operation" around the country but were working to identify to those responsible for disorder.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Firework Control Zones (FCZs) - where it is an offence to set off fireworks - are in place in 14 areas in Edinburgh and four in Glasgow until early November, and dispersal zones are in force in some places.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: On Halloween there were reports of fireworks lit in the street and some thrown at members of the public in Glasgow, Tranent in East Lothian and Bonnyrigg in Midlothian.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Police said no officers were injured and inquiries to identify those involved were ongoing.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Operation Moonbeam, which runs up to the evening of 5 November, means police can call on specially trained officers to deal with violence and disorder.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: It is the annual police response to firework-linked criminality, which is now in its ninth year.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: This year, FCZs banning the use of pyrotechnics in certain areas run from 30 October to 8 November in Edinburgh and until 9 November in Glasgow.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Seven dispersal orders were also issued in Edinburgh and work was ongoing to establish the number issued in Glasgow that relate to Operation Moonbeam.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: Ch Supt David Robertson said: "The overwhelming majority of Scotland's communities have celebrated Halloween in the proper spirit and I'm really grateful for the support of our efforts tonight to deter criminality, respond to reports of disorder and protect the public and emergency services from harm.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: "Sadly, however, we have again experienced incidents of fireworks used as projectiles at buildings, vehicles and members of the public.
sentences.article_title: Police tackle 144 Halloween fireworks incidents across Scotland

sentences.text: "This type of behaviour is completely unacceptable and has to stop before there are serious consequences." He said investigations would be launched immediately and Operation Moonbeam officers would continue to support local policing teams on fireworks-related crime over the next week.

sentences.text: Eleanor Hazel Aldred-Owen was 21 months old when she died at Alder Hey Hospital A hospital trust has taken full responsibility for 24 failures that led to the death of a 21-month-old.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Eleanor Hazel Aldred-Owen died at Liverpool's Alder Hey Hospital on 2 October 2023 - a coroner concluded she died as a result of misadventure, contributed to by neglect.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: She had routine surgery for craniosynostosis , external , a birth defect affecting the skull, but an abnormal chest X-ray was not flagged.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Eleanor suffered a cardiac arrest and an unsurvivable brain injury, and died in her parents' arms.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Her family, from Mold, Flintshire, said they had lived with "unbearable" guilt and trauma ever since.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Alder Hey Children's Hospital NHS Foundation Trust said her "tragic" death "should not have happened".
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Eleanor's dad Chaz said: "Not knowing how or why Eleanor died was the key factors and what kept us going was justice for her.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "The real victory is making sure what happened to Eleanor doesn't happen to anyone else.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: No other family or child will have to go through what we have." He added both he and his wife Rachel were "fairly certain it was neglectful" but did not realise the extent of it, and were "at the mercy of what Alder Hey were telling us".
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "They said it was breach of duty and not gross neglect and it took a long time for the trust to admit that." He said the trust "being compelled to admit gross neglect" was the hardest thing.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: During recovery, Eleanor had a raised heart rate and needed oxygen, and a decision was made to start AIRVO, a type of high-flow humidified oxygen, which was undocumented and not prescribed in accordance with the trust's guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: After her operation, Eleanor developed a collapsed lung as a result of surgery.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: A radiographer failed to flag her abnormal chest X-ray to anyone on the ward, and the doctor did not review it immediately because she was in A&E reviewing another child.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Eleanor had a cardiac arrest before the collapsed lung was identified and treated, causing an unsurvivable brain injury.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: An investigation found there were 24 failures in care that resulted in her death.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: These included failure to correctly calculate her Paediatric Early Warning System , external score on several occasions, which would have led to a much earlier medical review and chest X-ray.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: In a statement, her family said: "Eleanor's death was preventable and should not have happened.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "As parents, the guilt is unbearable, even though we know Eleanor was failed by the trust and not by us.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: We are irreversibly changed as people.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "We don't just constantly grieve for her, we grieve for the people we used to be when our daughter was here." They said they recognised the changes the trust has implemented following Eleanor's death, but that these had to be "used properly, kept under review and make care safer for other children".
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Chaz said two post-operative procedures had been brought in to Alder Hey and named after Eleanor, and the changes the hospital had put in place was Eleanor's legacy and something he and his wife could be proud of.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Lynda Reynolds, the family's solicitor and partner at Hugh James, said it was "an unimaginably tragic case".
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "Eleanor's parents placed their trust in Alder Hey Children's Hospital to care for their daughter and were let down," she said.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "For Eleanor's family, the trust's acceptance of responsibility and public apology are important, but this follows a long and painful process.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "We hope that the changes the trust have implemented continue to make care safer for other children." Eleanor's parents Rachel and Chaz say their lives are empty without their little girl Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust said "the shocking loss of Eleanor has left a permanent mark on us all".
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: The trust accepted full responsibility for these failures , external and said it was profoundly sorry they resulted in Eleanor's death.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: Chaz said he did not want Eleanor to be forgotten and to be remembered for the person she was, not how she died.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: "She was happy, strong and funny.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: She loved music and water.
sentences.article_title: Hospital admits full responsibility for 24 failures that led to toddler's death

sentences.text: She loved us and we loved her," he said.

sentences.text: George Russell (left) and Lewis Hamilton are the two drivers who can prevent Kimi Antonelli sealing the world title this weekend Lewis Hamilton has claimed his first pole position for Ferrari and his first for more than three years at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
sentences.article_title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix

sentences.text: The seven-time F1 champion beat Mercedes' George Russell by 0.009 seconds as the two drivers who can potentially stop Kimi Antonelli clinching the world title on Sunday locked out the front row.
sentences.article_title: Hamilton takes first pole for Ferrari at Mexico City Grand Prix

sentences.text: Antonelli qualified fifth behind Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, but will start fourth because of a one-place penalty for the Dutchman.

sentences.text: The only way Antonelli can be prevented from winning the title is if Russell wins and the Italian finishes lower than ninth, or if Hamilton wins and Antonelli is out of the points.

sentences.text: Hamilton's pole is his first since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, three years and three months ago, and the 105th of his career.

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood is expected to announce her final decision on immigration rules for legal migrants next week.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: She had proposed to extend the wait for permanent settlement from the current five years to 10 with some lower-paid migrants facing a 15-year wait.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: Mahmood has faced opposition from within the government for proposing to impose new rules on migrant workers already in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: Before she rejoined the cabinet, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner described the proposals as "un-British" because they sought to change the rules for people who had come to the UK in good faith.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: In particular, many lower-paid social care workers were facing a wait of up to 15 years rather than five.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: But the BBC understands that social care workers already in the UK are now likely to be exempt from the longer wait.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: But as originally proposed, it is likely most other workers will have to live and work in the UK for 10 years before being eligible for permanent settlement.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: That can be reduced if they contribute to their local communities or have higher incomes.
sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.article_title: Mahmood expected to announce changes to rules around indefinite leave to remain

sentences.text: This year the city celebrated four decades of its Halloween festival The 40th anniversary of Londonderry's Halloween festival has come to a spectacular close, with a carnival parade and fireworks display lighting up the skies over the River Foyle.
sentences.article_title: Fireworks and fancy dress at Derry's 40th Halloween festival

sentences.text: From its humble beginnings in the 1980s, the festival has grown to become what organisers have called Europe's largest Halloween celebration.

sentences.text: This year, Derry marked four decades of the festival with events inspired by folklore, mythology and the traditions of Samhain, the ancient Celtic festival from which Halloween has its roots.
sentences.article_title: Fireworks and fancy dress at Derry's 40th Halloween festival

sentences.text: Now a major fixture in the city's calendar, the final day of the festival attracted visitors from around the world, who joined in the celebrations with all of the ghosts, ghouls and goblins.

sentences.text: The parade drew thousands of people into the city centre A number of 40th birthday cake floats were used as part of the festival Saturday's programme featured events across the city and district, culminating in the traditional carnival parade with costumes, floats, music and dance performances.
sentences.article_title: Fireworks and fancy dress at Derry's 40th Halloween festival

sentences.text: Thousands of revellers then lined up along the riverfront to watch the dazzling fireworks display to mark the close of the festival's 40th year.

sentences.text: Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI).
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Alphabet's stock market value fell sharply on Thursday, taking more than $500bn (£374bn) off its market value after it revealed the AI summaries it now provides as the top answer to search queries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: At the same time, Alphabet expects to spend up to $205bn this year on investments, almost entirely related to AI.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere however, with Intel shedding more than $130bn in value.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The chip maker said it planned to increase spending on AI despite weaker demand for computers, a major source of demand for its micro-processors.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect to bring in more cash than it spent this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: In the earnings call, he said the firm had significantly ramped up investment in equipment in the third quarter and expected that to be "even more significant" in the following three months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Amazon on Thursday revealed it had also spent more cash than it was making, and that spending had increased six-fold over the span of three months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The company has committed to spending $220bn this year, putting the money towards investments such as AI data centres, network equipment, and servers.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Amazon shares recovered some overnight losses, but were still down by 1.4% at the end of Friday trading.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Reddit stock plunged by 29%, after the social media platform revealed weaker-than-expected daily user figures and warned that Google's growing AI-driven search was hurting referral traffic.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Stock in online game platform Roblox also fell, down by 18%, as its daily active user numbers dropped.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Several major tech firms have reported earnings this week, including Microsoft, and analysts said there were questions about the payout from the huge investments in AI.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Chris Low, from investment management firm FHN Financial, said the bulk of what was happening in the stock market was in reaction to some of the biggest tech players such as Amazon and Google.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: He told Reuters the companies were "showing some pretty significant growing pains as they aggressively pursue the AI build-out".
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "The thinking is that these signs suggest that the entire sector is going to slow down." Many analysts have been debating the possibility of an AI bubble in the stock market.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: The worry is that some tech firms will not be able to justify their sky-high valuations because the cost of building AI data centres and developing the software will end up being greater than the money they can make from it.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Kathleen Brookes, research director at trading firm XTB, said there have been many ups and downs in AI trade in recent months.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "Investors have turned ruthless, punishing any signs of disappointment in [third quarter] earnings," she said.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "The AI trade has had a good run in recent years, but now investors want payback, and companies like Alphabet and Intel are in the crosshairs." However, stock market values for many of these companies remain well above where they were a year ago.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: While the Nasdaq closed 2.8% lower, it is up 7.8% over the last year.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Similarly Amazon is up nearly 8% over the past 12 months, while Alphabet is down 1.3%.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: Brookes noted that November is typically a strong month for stocks.
sentences.article_title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn

sentences.text: "If we see AI stocks continue to struggle in the coming days, it could suggest the AI trade is past its peak, and investors will be looking for a new theme to drive markets," she said.

sentences.text: Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the UK's most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The 57-year old is the first Black person to oversee the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The City of London Corporation is an administrative body with responsibility for London's central financial district, headed by its own Lord Mayor.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas tops the 2027 Black Powerlist, which recognises the most powerful people of African and Caribbean heritage in the UK.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The award body said he was "a respected public-service leader with over 30 years' experience in local government".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Other influential names in this year's top ten include entrepreneurs Emma Grede and Steven Bartlett, as well as actor and filmmaker Sir Idris Elba.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Comedian Sir Lenny Henry has also been recognised, with a Lifetime Achievement award, for co-founding Comic Relief, which has raised over £1.6bn since 1985.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Now in its 21st year, the Black Powerlist celebrates people who have broken through barriers to reach leadership roles, thereby inspiring future generations.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "It exists to show young people of African and Caribbean heritage what is possible, in fields they might never have considered," said Michael Eboda, the list's publisher.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: As chief executive, he oversees around 5,000 staff with responsibilities including the City of London Police, 11,000 acres of open spaces such as Epping Forest and Hampstead Heath, and advocacy for the UK's financial and professional services sector.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas was born in Sheffield to parents who made the city their home after leaving Jamaica as part of the Windrush generation.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "They worked incredibly hard and instilled that sense of discipline and respect, and that's the core of how I do business," he said of his upbringing.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Growing up, Thomas aspired to be a footballer and took part in trials alongside Alan Shearer.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Reflecting on his own change of direction, Thomas joked it was about "following dreams and if they don't come true… there's always something else".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Before joining the City of London Corporation, Thomas served as chief executive of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames where he oversaw public services and a £1.2bn regeneration programme.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: He was appointed a CBE in the 2019 New Year Honours in the wake of the Rotherham Abuse scandal for transforming children's services during his time as strategic director for children and young people at Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas replaces last year's incumbent, Afua Kyei, the Bank of England's chief financial officer and executive director, and is joined on this year's list by Comfort Ero, the President and chief executive of the International Crisis Group, who takes second place.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: But now the West Midlands-based retailer is teetering on the edge , after its US-based owners Gordon Brothers cut off a vital funding supply and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group.

sentences.article_title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant

sentences.article_title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant

sentences.article_title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant

sentences.article_title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant

sentences.text: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist .
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected".
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Who could be behind the Binance hack and what we know so far Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens.

sentences.text: The Binance hack spooked cryptocurrency markets on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase was down 12% as investors also reacted to earnings results in which the firm reported revenue slightly below expectations.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Robinhood, a financial services company that trades in cryptocurrency, was down 7.8%.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: A lot of the fear right now from Binance users - and the crypto industry at large - is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm.
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry.

sentences.text: Several experts have warned customers not to regard Binance's promise to cover losses as legally binding and said they may need to pursue litigation to recover them.

sentences.text: Daniel Tunkel, of the London-based Edwin Coe law firm, said that would "come down to what [customers] have been promised in their contracts", and "where Binance can be sued for non-performance, if it comes to it".
sentences.article_title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea

sentences.text: At a workshop run by Levi's, Nicholas (r) says he prefers mending not to show, while Bianca (centre) says people still see it as a sign of poverty If Alice Brown is browsing in second-hand shops and finds a jumper with a hole, that won't stop her buying it.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: "I see it as challenge," says the 27-year-old forest ranger from Lincolnshire.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: She is a champion of the growing fashion for eye-catching repairs.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Over the last year she has developed her own unique style, needle-felting cute animals and insects to cover moth holes, stains and other imperfections, winning her a huge following online.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: "The natural place for decoration is in the centre at the front.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: If the hole is under the arm or on the shoulder, it forces you to think about the design," she says.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Often dubbed "visible mending" the trend is spreading from hobby crafters and community workshops, even drawing in fast-fashion brands and reaching the designer catwalks this year.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Some mends are designed to be eye-catching At one Saturday morning workshop in Brighton, Jayne Eagle shows her students how to attach a patch of fabric behind a tear so the cat-face design peeps through.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Then she instructs them in stitching techniques inspired by the traditional Japanese methods Boro and Sashiko.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Instead of matching the thread colour to the garment, they make the mend highly decorative using geometric patterns in large white stitching.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: She also offers classes in darning using contrasting vibrant colours that celebrate, rather than disguise, the repair.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Jayne Eagle sees repair as an "act of rebellion" against fast fashion One student, Nicola, has already used her newfound skills to stitch over sunscreen marks on a T-shirt "making a feature of it" and is now delighted that people "stop seeing the stains and just see the decoration".
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Another student, Lisa, says her mother's generation would never have wanted the mends to show.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: "Now part of it is being proud of what you've done," she says.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Lisa bought a second-hand jacket online, but snipped the fabric with the scissors when she was opening the package.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: She managed to patch it in a way that "looks intentional".
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: "I was actually pointing it out to people," she laughs.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Lisa says she's so proud of her mends she wants people to notice them In the past mending was primarily about saving money, by wearing clothes for longer, rather than buying new.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: But visible mending is about celebrating that choice.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: The trend took off about six years ago, Jayne says, and has boomed since.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: An era of "throwaway" fast fashion from the 1980s onwards undermined the tradition of looking after and mending your clothes and people lost the skills, she says.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: The revival of interest feels to her like a backlash against overproduction in the fashion industry and the damage it causes: the pollution, carbon emissions, water use, and poor labour conditions.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: Other High Street chains are adopting a more authentic approach, offering in-house repairs and workshops.
sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.article_title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.

sentences.text: Choosing the right moment to harvest can be a make-or-break decision When the first day of the apple harvest rolled around in Washington State last year, the fruit was ripe and the pickers were ready – but the weather had other ideas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It was like 38C… it's not safe for people to work in that heat," recalls Joel Carter at Okanagan Specialty Fruits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We had to stop at 10 o'clock in the morning." He says that artificial intelligence (AI) models that forecast ideal harvest dates, taking into account the weather, would be useful.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "You need to know more than just when your fruit is going to be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: How long do you have to pick it?" he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "That's where these models are really helpful." Carter's company has more than 1,250 acres of apple orchards in Washington, and the fruit is grown for sliced apple portions – often sold to hotels and schools, for example.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The firm is investing in technology with the hope of maximising productivity.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Even the apples are genetically engineered so that they don't brown easily once cut.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But planning a harvest is tricky.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: New tools that count and analyse fruit on the tree or vine, and predict when crops will ripen, are emerging.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: It matters because prices for fruit, especially high-value berries such as strawberries or blueberries can fluctuate wildly.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Getting the harvest date wrong means you book seasonal workers when you don't actually need them, and risk missing out on the biggest profits.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Okanagan Specialty Fruits is already experimenting with cameras from a Canadian firm called Vivid Machines.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The cameras are mounted atop tractors and they scoop up imagery of the apple trees as the tractor trundles by.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: AI identifies buds, flowers or fruit in that footage.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Right now, Vivid is telling us crop estimates and harvest dates," says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He notes that the system is good at picking out very tiny flower buds, which are hard to see at a glance with the naked eye.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But the accuracy of forecasts is noticeably dependent on the quality of historical information fed in to the system, adds Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "This isn't something where an AI can scrape the internet and figure out what's the average [yield] for Granny Smith," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "It's going to be bespoke to your farm." Apples are at least somewhat forgiving – the harvest window for those Granny Smiths is three weeks long, says Carter.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: For other fruit, such as berries, you might only have a few days.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "If a strawberry crop is on, you have to harvest it – otherwise your entire crop gets diseased very, very quickly," says Raymond Martin, co-founder and chief operating officer of FruitCast, a UK company that offers harvest forecasts to fruit growers here.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: His firm offers growers crop predictions for strawberries and also raspberries, blackberries, blueberries and tomatoes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We're moving on to grapes next year," adds Martin.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Don't experienced farmers know when their fruit will be ripe, I ask?
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Martin says they generally do – but not necessarily across their entire farm, which might be many acres in size, or have both outdoor and indoor growing areas.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "We do exactly what the farmers could do but we just do it on a scale that they can't." The system analyses footage of ripening fruit that can be captured by drones, someone walking up and down a field with a smartphone, or a camera mounted on a farm vehicle.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This year has been challenging, notes Martin, with hot weather and severe drought hitting much of the UK .
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: This has stressed many fruit plants, putting them into thermal dormancy and slowing down fruit production.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: There's only a small window for picking berries says Raymond Martin The FruitCast model accounts for weather and irrigation conditions in its forecasts.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The company says, "our forecasts land within 10% of actual picked volume one week out (90% accurate) and within 17% three weeks out (83% accurate).
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: We guarantee less than 20% error…" Angus Soft Fruits is one company that has worked with FruitCast.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Yasaman Ghasempour (left) is developing ripeness detection techniques Researchers are also exploring new ways of analysing fruit in intense detail.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Many farmers already use handheld brix meters to gauge the sugar content of their crop.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: These devices work by measuring how much light has changed direction, or refracted, after passing through a liquid – indicating the volume of solids present.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Some such meters use infrared light, meaning there's no need to cut into the fruit to take measurements.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But Yasaman Ghasempour at Princeton University says millimetre waves, high frequency radio waves, can penetrate deeper "They basically respond very well to humidity, water [and sugar]," she says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: She and her students have come up with a millimetre wave-based ripeness detector , external that could be used by farmers – or even customers searching for perfectly ripe fruit in shops.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Her students tried it out at a local market in New Jersey.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "[Staff] there got kind of scared that we were doing something shady," laughs Ghasempour.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Such fine-grained analysis of fruit, if currently unripe, could also help inform forecasts of when it will be ripe.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Jing Zhang says new tech has to prove its worth to farmers But while some growers, such as Carter, are interested in trying out new tech, many will wonder whether investing in it is really worthwhile.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Adoption is very complicated," says Jing Zhang at North Carolina State University.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "The grower has to have confidence in the research and whether or not it works." Zhang has been working on a system to automatically count the number of blueberries , external captured in smartphone images of blueberry bushes.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: The simplest systems need not be expensive.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Kevin Wang at the University of Florida has developed another crop-counting tool that can harvest imagery , external from $100 (£74) drones.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: In the future, such information could feed in to ripeness predictions.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: However, he points out that some farmers might be uneasy about sharing commercially sensitive information about their growing strategies, such as fertiliser and irrigation plans, with third parties and AI models.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Ben Palone is senior director of automation and commercialisation at Western Growers, an association that represents farmers in the western US.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: He says harvest forecasts have some potential as "an optimisation tool".
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: But farmers will likely continue to rely on human intelligence.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: "Growers like to have people in the mix to make some of those very critical decisions – especially when it comes to harvests," he says.
sentences.article_title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have both spoken of their desire for the benefits bill to come down, but the government has not yet laid out a timetable for any reductions.

sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), estimates in its latest forecasts that the cost of the welfare system will rise , external from £353bn this year to £431bn in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The OBR's figures include spending on pensioners, which accounts for just under half of the total.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The majority of this cost is on the state pension.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, if we look at the size of welfare spending relative to the size of the overall economy the OBR's projections are less dramatic, increasing from 11.1% today to 11.3% of GDP in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Total welfare spending would also remain below the peak of around 12% of GDP in 2013 following the global financial crisis, leading some economists and researchers to question the idea that welfare spending is out of control. , external But there are some welfare costs that are rising rapidly.
