sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Accounting for inflation, spending on working-age disability benefits increased from £14bn in 2020 to £25bn in 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: So spending in some parts of the system has come down while it has risen in others - and there could be a connection.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Some researchers think the post-2010 welfare cuts to benefits might have created an incentive for people to claim sickness and disability benefits instead to protect their living standards , external , therefore shifting costs around the system rather than generating lasting savings.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Many also see a specific problem regarding the growing number of young people in the welfare system claiming benefits, including PIP.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: He added: "People in Newquay don't want politicians driving division.

sentences.text: They want someone who'll fix the roads, protect our coast, fight for local services and bring people together.

sentences.text: Labour is where I believe I can do that best, and I'm looking forward to getting on with the job." Councillor Kate Ewert, Labour and Co-operative Group Leader on Cornwall Council said Creek's decision "highlights the serious questions about Zack Polanski's leadership".

sentences.text: HM Treasury says it accepts a coroner's concerns after Chloe Moffat, the PA to one of its directors, took her own life The Treasury has accepted it contributed to the death of a personal assistant and said "immediate steps" have been taken to tackle outstanding risks.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: Chloe Moffat, 26, took her own life in May 2025, the day after managers told her of allegations that she had shared sensitive confidential information, which she denied.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: A coroner found a practice within HM Treasury of "informal fact-finding" meetings with employees accused of misconduct had no basis in the ministry's policy and posed a risk of future death.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: Responding, the Treasury and the Cabinet Office wrote that they "accept the concerns identified" and "take them extremely seriously".
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said it would also undertake a wider review of workplace conflict and resolution across Whitehall within a year.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: At Moffat's inquest in August, the Treasury was found to have "materially contributed" to her death by not telling her that the likely penalty if allegations against her were proven would be a written warning and not dismissal.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: In a response to the coroner's report , external , the Treasury "accepted the findings in the report in full" and said it had taken immediate action to mitigate the concerns raised.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line Strengthened "wellbeing safeguards" had been introduced and the use of informal fact-finding meetings had been stopped while a full policy review was conducted, the department said.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: Employees facing misconduct allegations would be informed of the possible outcomes before being asked to respond and a suicide prevention framework was being developed, it added.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: "HM Treasury has considered these concerns carefully and has taken immediate steps to mitigate the identified risks," according to the department's response.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: "While this work introduces some enhancements, much of it is intended to strengthen, clarify and build on the procedures and support already in place." A Treasury spokesperson added: "The Treasury's deepest sympathies continue to be with Chloe's friends and family, and the department continues to mourn our colleague.
sentences.article_title: Treasury accepts role in staff member's death

sentences.text: "An independent review found staff acted in good faith and with a duty of care throughout." Additional reporting by the Press Association Follow BBC Surrey on Facebook , external , on X , external , and on Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Surrey on Sounds .

sentences.text: Lord Kinnock says UK Labour decisions led to "dislike" of the Welsh arm of the party Former Labour leader Neil Kinnock says the party's welfare policies turned disillusionment with Labour in Wales into "active dislike".
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: He said that UK government decisions on benefits and winter fuel payments had driven voters in Wales away from the Welsh arm of the party before the country's Senedd election in May.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Lord Kinnock made the comments as part of a Newyddion S4C , external YouTube special on Andy Burnham's first 100 days as prime minister.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Governing "at both ends of the M4" before Wales' parliamentary elections had presented an extra challenge for his party, he said.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Winter fuel payments fell by 9.3 million before U-turn He said: "If there is any opposition or resentment to the government on either end of the M4, the other lot are going to pay as well.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: "There is no doubt in my mind," he said, that "alienation... had been creeping up".
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: "It could be a mixture of boredom.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: It could be a mixture of dislike," Kinnock said.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: He said "what turned that into active dislike" had been things "like the withdrawal of the winter fuel allowance, the threats to the welfare system" and not scrapping a cap on two child benefits quick enough.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: In June last year, the Labour UK government U-turned on its controversial decision to means-test winter fuel payments for pensioners in England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Almost one year later, Labour lost power in Wales in a seismic election in May , returning just nine Senedd members after running the Welsh government for 27 years.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Lord Kinnock, who is the father of Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock , also said he had reservations about devolving justice to Wales - a key demand of the Plaid Cymru Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Plaid ministers say it would allow for a more effective system tailored to Welsh communities and better integrated with health, housing and education.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: Kinnock said there would no be "much of an argument" against the idea if it meant that "Wales was better protected, that the streets were safer" and "that the justice system was more efficient".
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: "But those guarantees are absent at the moment," he said.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: "Until they exist, until they're in place, the upheaval of creating what would have to be effectively a new system with new management... with an introverted view of the justice system - there would be more downsides than upsides.
sentences.article_title: Winter fuel cuts turned the Welsh against Labour, former leader Neil Kinnock says

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Parliament's live broadcast showed the moments surrounding the alleged incident A war of words has broken out between Lib Dem MP Caroline Voaden and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage over an alleged physical altercation in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The row was triggered when Farage, explaining why he had not attended Wednesday's Budget, said he had been involved in a "physical altercation" with another MP at the State Opening of Parliament in May and had wanted to avoid a similar incident.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: Voaden revealed herself to be the MP Farage had been referring to, writing on social media that she had been left "shocked and bloody angry" by the confrontation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The Lib Dems have claimed that Farage "attempted to shove" their South Devon MP but a Reform source accused the party of "lying".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The Reform insider added: "The Lib Dems were claiming Nigel shoved her and that she was shaken, the video disproves that clearly." Footage, first unearthed by the Daily Telegraph, shows the pair leaving the chamber together at the state opening of Parliament but there is no visible evidence of a major altercation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: However, Voaden has said the incident between herself and Farage was not shown in the clip originally posted by the Telegraph , external .
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The incident does not appear to have been captured on the official feed of the state opening provided by Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: Voaden said Farage had been ordered to apologise to her after she complained to Commons authorities.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The House of Commons would not comment on this.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: In a statement, Voaden said: "The truth is that on the day of the King's Speech, Farage missed his chance to process with the other party leaders to the Lords, and rather than queue with the rest of us, he shoved me out of the way to barge past.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: "Such behaviour is unacceptable in any workplace, and it has no place in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: In response he said: "At the State Opening of Parliament, I got involved… I didn't want to… but I got involved in a physical altercation with an MP in the chamber.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: "I didn't make a fuss about it, I didn't complain, but I could see given that my prayer card had been removed, I was heading towards another physical altercation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the House of Commons said that a prayer card for Farage - the way in which MPs reserve seats in the Commons - did not "display a valid date stamp" and therefore "was removed in line with the usual Chamber protocol".

sentences.text: Andy Burnham and Rhun ap Iorwerth met in Glasgow on Friday Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth says there has been a "significant step forward" with regards to his country's spending and borrowing powers after meeting the prime minister.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Andy Burnham held a meeting of his National Economic Council with the first ministers of Wales and Scotland on Friday, after which ap Iorwerth said it was a matter of "how and when" a loosening of financial restrictions will take place.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: At the summit in Glasgow, Burnham lobbied the government leaders to devolve "deeper" to the regions of Wales and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: The prime minister said the two first ministers had agreed to work with him on "regional empowerment".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: No timescales were announced for changes to Wales' finances.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Friday's meeting followed rows between the Welsh and UK government over the chancellor's Budget on Wednesday, which ap Iorwerth had said was "not serious about Wales".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: His party Plaid Cymru said the budget left the Welsh government with a real-terms cut in funding, which the UK government denied.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth, John Swinney, joined by Welsh Finance Minister Elin Jones, attended the meeting on Friday Ap Iorwerth had set out a range of demands to the prime minister in a letter sent at the start of October.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: As well as calling for powers over policing and justice, and for more funding for rail projects, he called for an end to restrictions on access to the Wales reserve - spare funding that the Welsh government can store in one year to use in another.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: It is capped at £385m, and the Welsh government can only draw down £137.5m and £55m for resource and capital spend respectively per year.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: The Welsh government can also borrow up to £1.1bn for infrastructure, with a limit of £165m a year.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth said: "There were some real positives here.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "On fiscal flexibility, the ability for us to use our funding better in Wales, use our reserves better in Wales - and on borrowing powers, I was told clearly that its now was a matter of how and when.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: That is a significant step forward." He said there was "clearly an interest" for the prime minister to "really understand that sheer injustice of underfunding of rail in Wales that we have seen for many years".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "That is a particular issue we will be taking forward now between my office and his," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: On policing, the first minister said "I think instinctively the prime minister wants to go there and there's still work to do".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: At a speech this month the first minister called for "practical agreement" on how the two governments could work together on the economy, calling for Westminster to avoid duplication in areas that are devolved already to the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Burnham said Friday's meeting was "positive", and that both first ministers had agreed to "work together jointly on regional empowerment in Scotland and Wales as well".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "We now have a process where we have detailed work by officials on both sides to see if we can come to a set of arrangements that are right for Scotland and right for Wales," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "We had a good discussion today on two fronts, one around re-industrialisation and the offer of more devolution of innovation funding to the regional level." He said it was for Scotland and Wales to decide how that looks.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Burnham also said the UK government will now look at arrangements for further devolution of employment support.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock fiscal flexibilities and borrowing was on the agenda for future Welsh government discussions with No 10 North.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "It is going to take some conversations on how that would work in practice.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "I can't give you a specific time frame as things stand," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Following Wednesday's Budget, which saw an extra £450m announced for Wales over the next three years as well as funding for individual projects, the Welsh government claimed the extra money would represent a real-terms cut to its own finances.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: A £30m funding pledge for a new railway station in Cardiff was also described as "an insult" by Wales' transport minister.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: On Radio Wales Breakfast on Friday before the summit, ap Iorwerth said there were "paltry sums of money coming on rail, when they've said there's £14bn on the way" and a "real terms cut in the money we have to spend on public services".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "The Budget was not serious about Wales," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: He said in another interview he could "only assume that the prime minister is holding something back".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth told BBC Wales that Wednesday's Budget had "so little mention" of his nation After the meeting, Downing Street said ap Iorwerth had "agreed to start a process to explore how each government could contribute to regional empowerment, reindustrialisation and achieving good growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "This would be a policy sprint led by No 10 North, involving officials from each government, to take this agenda forward," they said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth said in a statement: "There was an encouraging consensus that the fiscal and borrowing powers which have for so long put Wales at a disadvantage compared with other UK nations must be revised as a matter of urgency.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "I welcome the prime minister's comments that this is now a matter of how and when." Welsh ministers had called for changes to their borrowing rules and assurances that child poverty payments it wants to introduce would leave recipients' tax and benefits allowances unaffected.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: None of that was addressed in the Budget, although Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock has said "positive" talks were continuing regarding the child poverty payments.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Friday's meeting of the National Economic Council - a summit to help boost the UK economy - was due to be attended by the prime minister and all the devolved leaders.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: However, it emerged on Thursday that Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill would not be there after her attendance was blocked by her Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Since he became prime minister, Burnham has consistently spoken in favour of devolution.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Michelle O'Neill described the move as "reckless and irresponsible" and meant people in Northern Ireland "will not be represented" Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill has been blocked by the DUP from attending an economic summit involving Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The Sinn Féin vice-president and Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly were both invited to attend the National Economic Council in Glasgow on Friday with other devolved leaders.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The DUP leader Gavin Robinson confirmed that his party colleague Little-Pengelly will not participate in joint engagements with O'Neill and permission will not be granted for the first minister to operate on a solo basis.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The move follows unionist anger over Sinn Féin's involvement in protests which prevented a contentious Orange Order march in Portadown from passing along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road .
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Robinson was flanked by DUP assembly members as he spoke in the Great Hall at Parliament Buildings A meeting of the party's ruling officer committee was held earlier on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the first minister's "arrogance will have consequences", but O'Neill accused the party of being "reckless and irresponsible".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: "Her complaints today that she's frustrated from engaging with the British Prime Minister within the sovereign United Kingdom will so be it because her law breaking must have consequences," Robinson said.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: O'Neill said the DUP leader's comments were "arrogant and supremacist" adding that the DUP "is consumed with their own internal leadership troubles and divisions".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: She said she would be at the Assembly on Monday with her party colleagues to "keep showing up every day for people".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Earlier she described the move to block the meeting with the prime minister as "reckless and irresponsible" and meant people in Northern Ireland "will not be represented".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: "This is a reactive stunt, driven by the DUP's own internal pressures and electoral problems," she said in a statement posted online.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The prime minister revived the National Economic Council over the summer to encourage greater collaboration between the nations and regions.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Earlier Little-Pengelly said the concerns arising from O'Neill's conduct and the "anger and hurt felt by many people across Northern Ireland, cannot simply be ignored or minimised".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: She said the decision comes after stopping a separate planned engagement with the President of Ireland, Catherine Connolly.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: "I have requested a separate meeting with the Prime Minister to ensure Northern Ireland's interests, including the urgent budgetary and funding challenges facing the Executive, continue to be represented directly," she added.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant said it was "deeply frustrating" that the Northern Ireland executive would not be represented at the National Economic Council.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The Sinn Féin deputy leader has defended her involvement, saying it was the "right thing to do".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV) leader Jim Allister said "the DUP's sham response today was beyond pathetic" adding "the DUP is interested only in clinging to office, not principle".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Alliance leader Naomi Long said refusing to attend or preventing others from attending the meeting with the prime minister was reckless and put party interests ahead of Northern Ireland's economic future and the needs of the public.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: "Ultimately it's only going to make reasonable people here conclude that the largest unionist party simply doesn't want to make the status quo work," he added.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The DUP has been under pressure from unionist rivals and some within its own ranks over how to respond to the row over Drumcree.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Last week, DUP MP Carla Lockhart stepped down from the party's officer board over their leader Gavin Robinson not withdrawing Little-Pengelly to force O'Neill from their joint Stormont office.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: On Thursday Lockhart said she will follow her "own course" if the party does not seek to remove Sinn Féin's Michelle O'Neill as Stormont's first minister.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Robinson said that while O'Neill and her party colleagues "should be punished, that does not include punishing the rest of Northern Ireland".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: The Upper Bann MP, who last week quit the DUP's ruling officer board in opposition to party leader Gavin Robinson's approach, outlined her position in a letter to colleagues which she later posted on Facebook.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Other DUP representatives including assembly member Diane Forsythe have since backed Lockhart's calls for O'Neill to be "removed from office" .
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: On Tuesday, Forsythe said that in the absence of such "meaningful action", official engagements through the joint Executive Office should be stopped immediately as a "bare minimum".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: On Wednesday, a second DUP assembly member called for O'Neill to go.
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Maurice Bradley said removing O'Neill "would not, in itself, require the Assembly to collapse".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Carla Lockhart stepped down from the DUP's officer board last week Bradley added that the party "must stand together" and "support Carla Lockhart".
sentences.article_title: DUP blocks Michelle O'Neill's engagements over Drumcree

sentences.text: Other party members including former MP Lord McCrea and Mid Ulster councillor Clement Cuthbertson have also backed Lockhart.

sentences.text: People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Typical working-age households would see their disposable income fall by £1,050, or 3%, between now and 2029, according to the Resolution Foundation, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the current decade would be the worst for household income growth on record.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey said his Budget offered "breathing space", but said the government could "never remove completely" cost of living pressures.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The UK's official forecaster said its latest economic forecast painted a "pretty grim picture".
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), blamed the difficult financial situation facing the UK on higher borrowing costs and inflation caused by the US-Iran war.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: In response to rising energy prices, Healey has announced measures, including a £100 support payment, aimed at easing pressure on household finances.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: But that would not be enough to offset the impact of higher energy bills, the Resolution Foundation said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "This parliament is increasingly looking like one of two halves," said the think tank's chief executive, Ruth Curtice.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "The first half has been marked by rising living standards, solid economic growth and extra funding for public services," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: However, the second half of the parliament would be "tough going", she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Over the course of this parliament, incomes for non-pensioner households, after taxes, benefits, and housing costs are taken into account, will have risen by "a paltry" £600, the Resolution Foundation said, with the gains "already behind us".
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Even after the extra support provided by the government, households will be left paying higher energy bills than during the last energy crisis in 2022, according to its  analysis.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The Resolution Foundation said the support should have been more targeted at the poorest households.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Alongside the Budget the OBR issued its economic forecast indicating a slowdown in GDP growth from 1.2% in 2026 to 1% in 2027.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The forecast for next year is sharply lower than what was predicted at their last assessment in March.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The OBR also put its forecast for inflation for 2027 up from 2% to 3.4%.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Frozen tax thresholds are also eating into people's take-home pay.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: However, the OBR also emphasised the difficulties in economic forecasting, highlighting uncertainty over the future path of inflation, in particular, which could turn out to be either significantly higher or lower than their predictions.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: While the Resolution Foundation focused its forecast for living standards on working age households, the OBR looks at all households, including pensioners and reflects a 10-year rolling average growth to take into account short-term fluctuations.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The OBR found that by the end of the decade living standards for all households would have barely grown, by less than 0.1% per year.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Helen Miller, director of the influential think tank, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the outlook was "depressing".
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "This decade looks set to be the worst decade for growth in household incomes on record," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "No amount of temporary cost of living packages will fix that.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: We need a stronger economy." There would also be growing pressure on the government's spending plans over the parliament, Miller added.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "Spending plans look extremely tight.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: They don't look to me like plans that this government would want to deliver," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "Whether or not they are delivered matters because the spending plans underpin the plan to bring down borrowing," she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Miller said she was left with the impression that Healey was hoping the economy would improve to take the pressure off those spending decisions.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Healey, speaking on the BBC's Today Programme, said "economic storms", including the Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, were affecting countries around the world and the government was seeking to help where it could.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: He said energy bill help would create "breathing space" for most households.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Around 20 million households are set to receive the £100 payment based on which council tax band they are in.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: But Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the Budget had left the public finances "more fragile" as Healey had reduced the "headroom" or the buffer that the country has between what it takes in revenues and what it spends.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey said the £100 energy payment would be identified as the best item in the Budget for many people, but said that it was "not good enough" when you considered the "stealth tax rises" that were taking money out of people's pay packets.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Bereaved families will no longer be hit by an unexpected tax bill because of severe delays paying out civil service pensions, following a change in Wednesday's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Under previous HMRC rules, certain lump sum pension payments had to be paid within two years of the pension scheme being notified of a death to remain tax-free.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Campaigners had warned some families could face an unfair financial penalty because of delays which were not their fault.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: The government has now changed the rules so payments will no longer become taxable solely because more than two years has passed.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: The Civil Service Pension scheme manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Outsourcing firm Capita took over the administration of the scheme from a company called MyCSP in December 2025, saying it inherited a backlog of more than 86,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Despite a two-year transition period to prepare for the takeover, problems have persisted and by February the backlog had grown to 120,000 cases.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Retired civil servants and bereaved families have been left waiting months for pension payments, with some struggling to pay bills.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: According to the latest figures up to 30 September , external , 1,643 outstanding cases of bereavement or death in service are more than 100 days old.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office, which has overall responsibility for the Civil Service Pension Scheme, previously said only a small number of these cases were approaching the two-year threshold.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: However the PCS union, which represents civil servants, had warned there were "serious questions" over how long cases would remain unresolved.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: After his case was highlighted by the BBC last week, Rob says he got a call from the pension scheme's complaints department who told him the payment was on its way.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: However, because it was made after two years it was taxed at 45%, amounting to thousands of pounds.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: If the payment was made after the rule change, it would not have been subject to tax.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Rob told the BBC he was pleased the government had addressed the issue in the Budget as this would mean others in his situation would not face a tax bill.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: While he said he was happy to finally get his payment it was "a bitter pill to swallow" as he is now waiting for the outcome of a complaint review to find out if the tax will be reimbursed.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Bell said the move would "make the position fairer for all grieving families and friends where there are delays in the payment of death benefits, whether in the Civil Service or any other pensions scheme".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: However, the government has now removed the two-year deadline so payments will no longer become taxable solely because they were made more than two years after a pension scheme was notified of the death.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: The change applies to payments made from 28 October.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: In his letter, the pensions minister said people who had already been impacted by avoidable delays and been taxed as a result could seek compensation through the pension scheme's complaints process and the Pensions Ombudsman.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Sir Geoffrey welcomed the announcement but said it does not "absolve Capita from processing and making payments to members of this scheme in a timely manner".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Fran Heathcote, general secretary of the PCS union, also welcomed the change but said "this situation should never have arisen in the first place".
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: She added: "Bereaved families must not pay the price for failures in the pension system.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: "Capita is not off the hook, it continues to fail members and their families, which is why the scheme must be brought back in-house." Capita has previously apologised for the impact of delays on pension scheme members and their families.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: The company has said it is working to resolve outstanding cases as quickly as possible, with a particular focus on people who have been waiting the longest and those facing financial hardship or challenging circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Bereaved families will not face tax bill over pension delays under new rules

sentences.text: Tony Vaughan (pictured) has shown remorse, according to a report A Labour MP has said sorry in the House of Commons following complaints over his behaviour towards a female member of staff.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: It comes as the Independent Expert Panel published a report , external requiring Tony Vaughan to apologise for breaching Parliament's bullying and harassment policy.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The MP for Folkestone and Hythe was found by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards to have committed the breach after a constituency staff member complained he "behaved towards [her] in an overbearing and belittling manner".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan said on Thursday he accepted the findings in full.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "As a result of these behaviours, my former colleague was upset and humiliated," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "My behaviour had a real and continuing impact on her and her family, and I am truly sorry for this." The Labour Party said it "expects the highest standards of conduct from all our members and elected representatives.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "We have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "It is right that Tony Vaughan has apologised following this independent process," a spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan, who has represented his Kent constituency since 2024, was found to have hugged the complainant without consent at an office event.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: He also took her personal mobile phone from her hand to join an online meeting without asking permission and failed to explain why phone calls between them had ended abruptly.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan appealed the Commissioner's findings, though the Independent Expert Panel confirmed the majority of them, according to Parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The sub-panel stressed that "oppressive and bullying behaviour towards [MPs'] staff members is wholly unacceptable".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: It added that Vaughan's actions were breaches of "basic boundaries and courtesy" - rather than failures in management - and an "abuse of his power".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: MP apologises over bullying and harassment The politician told MPs on Thursday that he was not "sufficiently alert" to the power imbalances between him and his employee.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: He added he recognised his behaviour could well impact on "someone who is vulnerable whether or not that is known".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "I made mistakes," Vaughan continued.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The 36-page report said it took account of the impact of what happened on the complainant, who has a right to anonymity.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: She said she was left feeling stressed, exhausted and offended, it adds.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The report also stated that Vaughan had "expressed genuine and thoughtful remorse".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: He should be required to make an "unreserved apology" to the complainant and the House by way of a personal statement in the House of Commons Chamber, it continued.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "We consider that this achieves the appropriate balance and clear messaging required regarding the behaviour expected of MPs," the report said.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan added he had undertaken further training as a result of the incident.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Millions of households will get £100 to help with soaring energy bills to be paid for by a tax on bank profits, John Healey has announced in his first Budget.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: The chancellor said he wanted to give hard-pressed families "breathing space now" and "hope for the future" as the UK economy is battered by "global economic storms".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: He also unveiled tax breaks to boost high street businesses - but confirmed that many big decisions, including on defence spending and welfare, will not be made until next year.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said Healey's plans were "not bold enough" and the government was "overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: In an hour-long speech to a packed House of Commons, with Prime Minister Andy Burnham and other frontbench colleagues cheering him on, the chancellor unveiled a string of measures aimed at cutting the cost of living.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: One-off £100 energy payment for people living in council tax bands A to D in England, with Wales saying it will match the payment and the Scottish government planning to "replicate" it Gas standing charges in England, Scotland and Wales, to be scrapped during 2027 "or as soon as possible after".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: But he had little scope for big giveaways as the public finances remain stretched, with the UK set to spend £14bn more on debt interest payments this year.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Income tax thresholds will remain frozen and the tax on income from savings and property rental will rise to 24% for basic rate taxpayers from April 2027, after it had been scheduled to go up to 22%.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: But a cut to the cash ISA allowance from £20,000 a year to £12,000, announced last year by Healey's predecessor Rachel Reeves, will be axed.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) downgraded its growth forecast for next year to 1%, with slightly higher increases predicted for subsequent years.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: In its latest assessment, the OBR said British households were set to be little better off than before the Covid pandemic even a decade after Covid-19 hit, a situation the watchdog's boss David Miles described as "pretty grim".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: In his Budget speech, Healey repeatedly stressed that the UK economy was being battered by "global uncertainties" and soaring oil prices caused by conflict in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: "Those are the storms we face.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: We must choose the course we steer through them," he told MPs.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: What are the key points from the Budget and how will it be funded?
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Healey also used his speech to announce plans to allow regional mayors to keep 20% of business rates and a share of income tax to spend on local priorities.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: The aim was to allow mayors to retain 100% of business rates raised in their areas by the end of the decade, he added, in "the most radical act of devolution in a generation".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: And he sought to address opposition claims the Labour government is unwilling to cut benefits, insisting that both he and Burnham were committed to bringing down the welfare bill in a "Labour way".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: But he said no decisions would be taken until reviews by Alan Milburn , into young people not in work or training, and Stephen Timms, on Personal Independence Payments , had been published, with legislation to follow next year.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: The £4.7bn black hole in the defence investment plan will be funded, the chancellor revealed, in part through taking money from capital budgets across Whitehall.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Healey said he will set out how the government plans to meet its commitment to spend 3% of the national income on defence by 2030, and 3.5% by 2035, at next year's spending review.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: But Badenoch said he "should have set out a plan for 3% today," highlighting his claim when he resigned as Sir Keir Starmer's defence secretary in June that UK forces were at risk due to a lack of cash.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: "So now he is the man who is increasing risk to personnel on operations, he is the man who is making our country less safe, he has failed his own test," the Conservative leader said.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: "This is on him and no-one will ever forget.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: If he had any decency he would resign again today." The Tory leader said that with the UK heading for a record tax burden and "spending more on debt interest than on the army and schools combined", Healey's Budget was "not good enough, not strong enough, not bold enough".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Helen Miller, director of the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said the Budget "has a raft of fiddly measures but very little that will move the dial on growth".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said that until the government has "the courage" to fix the UK's trading relationship with the EU any Budget will just be "tinkering around the edges" and will not provide the growth the country needs.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said the Budget was full of "little giveaways" but  "doesn't overall do very much" and did not offer "anything of any value on defence whatsoever".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Healey also faced criticism from the left, with the general secretary of the Unite union, Sharon Graham describing the cost of living measures in the Budget as "baby steps".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: "Scrapping standing charges on gas and a £100 energy payment for households in council tax bands, A to D, whilst welcome, will not touch the sides, when many forecasts show bills set to jump over £400 in January," she added.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski said it was a Budget "that betrays the future for young people and the planet they inherit".
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: He added: "The chancellor didn't mention climate once but praised bankers repeatedly." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.
sentences.article_title: Healey unveils £100 for energy bills and bank tax in first Budget

sentences.text: While earnings are rising, forecasters predict that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes John Healey talked of charting a new course for Britain, but this Budget was more about course-correcting than charging down a new path.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: It was abundantly clear that the financial fallout from that conflict in the Middle East has hampered the finances of households and businesses – and the government's ability to help.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: While the government targeted those impacted by higher energy and fuel bills, the "breathing space" it aimed to provide was limited; it is a pill that doesn't fully alleviate the pain.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: The most telling evidence was that official forecasters predict that while earnings will rise, that is not compensating for higher prices and taxes.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: Even after the extra help is taken into account, households' incomes after inflation and tax are set to be typically lower across the next two years than the start of the parliament.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: On that basis, it could be the second worse parliament for living standards, after the last one, since the 1950s - a sign of how far the war has blown prosperity off course.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: But it can't be all be blamed on the war.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: Although there were few major measures aimed at households, the policy of previous chancellors of freezing the thresholds at which different rates of tax on income apply - fiscal drag - has been maintained in the background, scooping more money out of pay packets.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: Overall, this Budget has the tax burden - the proportion of the nation's income going to the tax office - rising to a new historic high of 38.6% However, a more generous package of help would have been hard to pull off.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: The impact of higher inflation and debt have increased borrowing costs by £14bn in the past year alone.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: The Chancellor had to prove to the markets which lend the government money that he has a plan to bring down future debt to avoid those costs climbing further.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: As it stands, debt interest repayments are due to be £160bn in 2032, more than double the amount spent on schools in England.
sentences.article_title: Healey provides some breathing space but things still set to get worse for most

sentences.text: And the plans Healey has unveiled already eat into wiggle room he has within the public finances.

sentences.text: Families facing cost-of-living pressures are being offered some help, or "breathing space" as Chancellor John Healey is calling it.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Here's how the key announcements in the Budget affect you and your money.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: If you are living in a home in council tax bands A to D in England, you will receive a one-off £100 "Household Energy Payment" from January, funded by extra tax on banks.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It will be paid directly into your bank account.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Council tax bands are listed below - you can check which one you are in by looking at your annual bill or checking the government's website , external , although that was struggling to cope with traffic after the announcement.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Administrations in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive the equivalent funding, and they will decide whether to introduce the same payment.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: This is designed to help with soaring energy bills, with some forecasts suggesting a typical annual bill could rise by £400 or so to £2,100 in January the saving will be only a portion of that.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Although it's designated for energy bills, you can spend the money on anything you wish.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The VAT cut on electricity bills, which was introduced in October, will also be extended to July.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: It was due to end in April.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: These fixed daily charges will then be shifted onto the price you pay for each unit of energy.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: The government wants to extend reforms to electricity standing charges later.
sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.article_title: Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you

sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say
