sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: "My low Vitamin D levels hit me like a truck" Twenty-three-year-old Saskia Reeves-Priestley was at work when she suddenly collapsed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I just felt really dizzy, really nauseous, was having heart palpitations and was really hot," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Saskia, a special educational needs teacher, was a keen goalkeeper who played football four times a week and felt fit and healthy.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Blood tests later showed her level was so low - it was "next to nothing".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Lower levels of sunlight - depending on where in the world you live or the time of year - decrease the body's ability to produce it.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Doctors don't routinely offer blood tests to check for vitamin D deficiency, but will offer a supplement if a patient is concerned they might be high risk.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In adults it causes a similar weakening of the bone called osteomalacia , external .
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "They call it the silent disease," says Dr Suma Uday, a paediatric endocrinologist who wants to raise awareness of the problem.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She warns that vitamin D deficiency in young people and adults is difficult to spot and can be missed or misdiagnosed.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Symptoms include fatigue and joint and bone pain.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday says: "It's basically silently eating away at the bones, leaving them softened and prone to breaks." Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "I couldn't really see in front of me," she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Her housemate took her to A&E - later she too would be diagnosed as vitamin D deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Other than feeling tired, she says she had no symptoms: "I'm a 21-year-old student.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: I've got work and uni - I'm always feeling tired." She remembers her mother suffering from low vitamin D but says she did not realise it could happen to her.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: After taking supplements, Amaka feels a lot better, but she is anxious in case it happens again.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "It was scary and I don't want to experience that again." Uday joins other clinicians and academics who have formed a group - ACT NOW Vitamin D - calling for the threshold at which you are classified as deficient to be raised.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: She says that would "catch" more people with low vitamin D and give a more accurate picture of how widespread the issue is.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: It would also mean they can treat the deficiency earlier, she says.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Uday warns of "a lifelong deficit" in women - in adolescence, then pregnancy, and then the newborn is affected.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If you don't correct it from the very beginning," she says, "this is going to affect multiple generations." Saskia Reeves-Priestley plays football four times a week - and had no previous symptoms "It's shocking," says Prof Martin Hewison, from the University of Birmingham.

sentences.text: He tells me that despite being 100 years on from the discovery of vitamin D "rickets hasn't gone away".
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: "If we have rickets in the community, there are going to be many more people who are vitamin D deficient." He says the government should look into wider fortification of food in which vitamins are added to foods during production.

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Tony Chapman, 75, from Corby in the East Midlands was one of the 1,100 melanoma patients enrolled on the vaccine trial A new personalised cancer vaccine given alongside a widely used immunotherapy drug has cut the risk of patients dying or their skin cancer returning by 42% in a major clinical trial.

sentences.article_title: First personalised cancer vaccine cuts risk of disease returning in major trial

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey unveiled his Budget on Wednesday This was a Budget I would describe as a flotilla of small measures.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Westminster is poring over the 150 page Red Book , external in which the Budget is printed and also what is formally called the Economic and Fiscal Outlook published , external by the watchdog and forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility, the OBR.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: The Red Book sets out the measures the chancellor will implement and how much they will cost.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: There are 98 of them, considerably more than normal and more than in either of Rachel Reeves' budgets.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: But nearly all of them are pretty small in terms of their impact on the Treasury's spreadsheets.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: This gets to the heart of why those involved in compiling this Budget have been irritated by commentary in the build up to it suggesting there would be nothing to see in John Healey's address – but also why those suggesting that were arguably onto something as well.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Firstly, as expected, it was a much smaller Budget in overall tax and spending terms than plenty of recent ones have been.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: But there were plenty of measures here and there which the chancellor will hope enough people notice and value – and others that some will likely curse.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: There are more taxes for savers and landlords, for instance, and too for banks.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: When a government has promised, as Labour have, to not put up income tax, national insurance or VAT – the big revenue generators – they end up looking elsewhere if they conclude putting up tax is necessary.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: That runs the political risk of choosing particular sectors who might respond rather noisily.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Think of the plenty of farmers who were incensed by the changes to inheritance tax Rachel Reeves was keen on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: And there is a recurring sense of déjà vu in the language of the OBR.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: "The UK's economic and fiscal position remains very challenging," it says, with a splash of understatement, adding that "there have been further adverse developments" this year with in the conflict in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: As for what happens, next, well, frankly, who on earth knows.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: What happens, for instance, in the Middle East, once the mid term elections are done in America and the result of the Israeli general election is clear?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: In short, the chancellor felt constrained in his capacity to act and his capacity to make a noticeable positive difference is perhaps constrained even more so – because any intervention, even expensive ones, may merely make a grim situation a bit less bad , rather than things actually feeling better.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Mitigating the bad is arguably a noble political aim, but it costs money and potentially comes with little political upside.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Instead there is this fleet of smaller measures that the government will hope gives their MPs something to try to sell – while acknowledging that they are not world changing.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Luke Tryl, the UK Director of the More in Common think tank, says: "The softly populist tone of this budget is likely to land well with the public.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: "Instead, by offering support to all of those on Council Tax bands A to D, he is able to reassure them that the government will support them too." The reaction of the opposition parties, from a range of different political perspectives, amounts to a critique that this Budget was thin.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: In summary, this felt like a cautious Budget.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Private companies buying up care homes for older people in England could undermine the government's plan to create a universal care service , the regulator says.

sentences.text: The Care Quality Commission's annual report , external highlights how a rising share of the care home market is owned by large firms - the five biggest increased their share by 26% in the last two years, driven by interest from US property investors, and now own one in seven homes.

sentences.text: While there can be benefits, there are concerns the trend can lead to higher prices and a reduction in quality.

sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: In contrast, there are few smaller care homes judged important for providing specialist and personalised care.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: Small care homes have always represented a tiny proportion of the care home market, but over the last 14 years the numbers have fallen significantly, particularly those that combine care with nursing support, which are down by a quarter.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: The CQC said the funding system remains fragile – people using care services either self-fund or, for the poorest, the state helps to pay for their costs.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: He said this government's renewed focus on social care – Andy Burnham made it one of his key priorities when he became prime minister – was welcome.

sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: "A clearer vision is needed," he added.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: Hugh Alderwick, of the Health Foundation think-tank, said the report by the CQC "lays bare the massive challenges" facing the government.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: "The prime minister's commitment to reforming the sector provides an opportunity to fundamentally redraw the state's offer on social care.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: "But change is needed now to strengthen the fundamentals of the system.
sentences.article_title: Rapid changes to care market risk to National Care Service, regulator says

sentences.text: "Unless we get some real progress in a funding settlement, the trend of smaller homes closing will be a trend that will continue." sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The settings will be "straightforward to set up" using a Pin set by a parent, which teens will need if they want to switch off the controls.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Parents can also choose how their teenager uses Channels, which allows organisations and public figures to send out content.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And they will have the option of choosing between the default 13+ setting for Meta AI, the app's optional built-in AI assistant, or a stricter "Limited Content" option.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "All of these controls are being designed to support open conversations about how to use WhatsApp between parents and teens, while keeping everyone's personal messages private," the company said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: The changes come as pressure mounts on tech companies from governments and regulators to change the way they operate in order to better protect children using their platforms.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In June, the government announced it plans to ban under-16s from social media platforms, with the restrictions expected to come into force in March 2027.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It said "highly effective age assurance" measures would be used to check the age of those using social media.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: WhatsApp is currently excluded from the ban because the government considers it a messaging service.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The university had a deficit of around £12.5m in the last financial year Staff at Queen's University of Belfast (QUB) have been warned of "difficult decisions" ahead due to the university's finances.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Pay deals with staff, and childcare and gym fees for staff and students are under review while staff car-parking charges are going up.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: The details came in an message to staff from the university's vice-chancellor Prof Sir Ian Greer.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: His message came after the grant paid by the Northern Ireland Executive to universities had a "significant" cut in 2025/26 .
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: According to Greer, the university had a deficit of about £12.5m in the last financial year.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: While the university hoped to reduce that, he said that a combination of cuts in funding from Stormont and a fall in student fee income meant the university had to "control costs".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: There have been tougher visa requirements for international students coming to UK universities in recent years.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: According to the university's annual accounts, the income QUB received from international student fees recently fell by around £5m - from more than £60m in 2024 to around £55m in 2025.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Greer also said that student recruitment income was expected to be around £7m "below target" in the current year.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: He said that the university still hoped to deliver agreed pay deals to staff.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "However, given the Department for the Economy's position, we have no choice but to keep the position under review," he said.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Ian Greer (left) with former US president Bill Clinton Some other charges, including for staff car-parking on campus are going up.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Costs for university services that staff and students use, like childcare and membership of the university Physical Education Centre (PEC) are also under review and may rise.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: However, plans for a new university heritage and visitor centre , external , to be built in the Quad on the site of the current administration building, are going ahead.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: But there may be more savings measures to come.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "The University Management Board has agreed to identify approximately £10m of savings this year and, depending on the final position with public funding, further difficult choices may have to follow this academic year," Greer said.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Greer said that due to a cap on student numbers, QUB had turned away "around 500 students who had the grades to attend Queen's".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: The number of local students both QUB and Ulster University (UU) can admit is decided by Stormont's Department for the Economy and depends on available funding.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: Current QUB students who use university childcare or the PEC may also face higher fees for the services.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: But Greer said that "the student experience must remain central to our decisions".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: In a further statement to BBC News NI, a QUB spokesperson said that the university was "facing increasing financial pressures arising from reduced public funding, lower student recruitment income and rising costs".
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: "Our planned approach is centred on both stability and growth, to secure the university's long-term future while supporting our students and staff," it said.
sentences.article_title: University staff warned of 'difficult decisions' ahead over finances

sentences.text: New vocational GCSEs will be introduced from 2029 for 14-year-olds alongside existing core academic subjects in England.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The new subjects could include building and construction, business management and finance, and child development.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said there was "no question" that academic learning was at "the core of any education system", but said there was "huge demand" for subjects with more practical elements too.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Education unions said the ideas were welcome, but a clear strategy was needed to make them happen.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The Conservatives said the plans risked "throwing away" progress made in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Standards for the new qualifications will be set nationally by the regulator Ofqual to ensure grades are in line with other GCSEs, and will gradually replace other qualifications at this level such as BTec tech awards.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The vocational GCSEs will be designed to allow teenagers to progress at 16 to studying similar courses at college, including the new V-levels , which schools and colleges are teaching from autumn 2027, and T-levels .
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: The idea is to create a clear pathway for teenagers into different types of work through a ladder of qualifications.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: But the Liberal Democrats warned the new vocational GCSEs should not become a "pipeline" directing disadvantaged pupils away from more academic subjects.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC she was "not going to oversee a two-tier education system".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: "I want working class, disadvantaged young people to have every opportunity to achieve highly academically," she said.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Asked whether there would be dedicated funding to help schools cover the cost of the new qualifications, she said the government would "work with the sector to make sure this is absolutely deliverable", and that ministers would "make sure any funding needed is made available".
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: A new national target for employers to help create 200,000 work experience opportunities for under-16s is also being set by Prime Minister Andy Burnham, as part of reforms to shake-up the education system to better prepare young people for the world of work.
sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Like a lot of other holidays, food often plays a big part in how people celebrate Halloween, but it can be a more complex to navigate if you have a food allergy - especially if you want to go to parties or take children trick or treating.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: How do people with allergies ensure they can take part in the fun and stay safe?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And how can you help make sure that everyone is included in the celebrations?
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, is allergic to milk and eggs.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "You have to make sure you read every packet of everything, and you couldn't eat anything until you got home so that you were safe and you were sure of what was happening," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: When it comes to Halloween, she said people having more awareness would mean that everyone could be included in the fun.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She says that her friend group really help her by knowing about her allergies and what to do if she was to have a reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Whilst she said it "wasn't easy" or a "particularly enjoyable" thing to do, she taught her group what to do in an emergency situation.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara, 15, went to a Halloween party this week dressed as Daphne from Scooby Doo Ciara carries EpiPens.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: These are adrenaline injections that can help to save people's lives in a serious allergic reaction.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: The 15-year-old explained that Halloween can be a bit more difficult to navigate.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She described how a lot of people are helpful and understanding about allergies but sometimes, "there are other people that just don't seem to fully understand the consequences" of what would happen if she was exposed to what she's allergic to.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Her mum, Claire McGuigan, said she is proud of how well Ciara deals with her allergy.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She explained that parents of children with allergies have all the usual worries but "first and foremost is your allergy".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "As a parent, you carry all that worry and you just hope that they go out and they have a nice time and they come back safe, full of fun, and they can forget about their allergies as much as they can for that night".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think having a good circle of friends who understands the allergies is important.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Trying to prevent the harm rather than relying on the rescue medication is really, really important," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Ciara's mum described the emotional burden on families and called for a national conversation about it.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said people who have children with allergies or have allergies themselves have to do their "best to navigate a whole world that wasn't designed for you".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "I think take your wins everyday that you're safe and that you're happy and don't let it define you.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: You can be who you want to be," she continued.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She believes that with "a bit of careful planning" children with allergies can feel included.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán in his Halloween costume Caolán has just turned 11.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: His mum Colette Donaghy said he does all the "school activities that you could name" and he's "mad into scooting".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán is allergic to nuts, dairy and eggs and has had, in the past, a very serious anaphylactic reaction that resulted in him being in an induced coma in intensive care.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "He has an awareness and a knowledge and probably a risk awareness that many other children of his age wouldn't have," his mum said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She thinks it's important that children with allergies are "understood" but not made  to feel "really different".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Caolán's mum, Colette Donaghy, said giving out individually wrapped sweets to trick-or-treaters could help avoid cross-contamination When it comes to Halloween, Donaghy explained that when Caolán trick or treats, he waits until the end when all the other children have been given their sweets.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Then he will explain to the people at the door that he has allergies and there's only certain things he can have.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: And then, of course, before he would eat anything, we would have to check it," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy advised giving out individually wrapped sweets to help avoid cross-contamination.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She also suggested looking at alternatives to sweets like fruit or little toys "that don't cost very much".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "There's loads of different options for people and that would take away another layer of anxiety for parents," she said.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Donaghy also explained how some people use teal pumpkins to indicate that a house will offer treats that are suitable for any trick-or-treaters who have any food allergies or intolerances.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Niamh Kennedy, from Food Allergy NI, said everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive Niamh Kennedy has three children who have food allergies and she is the chair of Food Allergy NI.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: It's a group aiming to build a safer and more inclusive society for everyone affected by food allergies.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said special occasions are often centred around food.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "For families living with food allergies, these celebrations can bring an extra layer of planning and worry that many people never have to think about." She explained that "every item may need to be checked and every situation assessed for risk".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: Kennedy suggests that everyone should "think ahead" to consider how they can make celebrations inclusive.
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: She said this may include "offering non-food alternatives, providing clear ingredient information, communicating with families in advance and being mindful of the risk of cross-contact".
sentences.article_title: How do you navigate Halloween with food allergies?

sentences.text: "Being thoughtful and understanding can make a real difference to whether someone feels left out or included in these occasions." sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: For students, previously contracts were generally for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Instead, properties are now rented on a rolling basis, which means tenants pay rent weekly or monthly with no fixed end date.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: University-owned halls of residence and Purpose-Built Student Accommodation are exempt , external and can still offer fixed-term contracts so this change primarily affects students renting from a private landlord.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If the Renters' Rights Act wasn't a thing, I don't think I would have been able to move universities because I would have been locked into the full [year] contract," Eddie explains.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Fortunately, Eddie had a friend who was looking for a room who was able to take his place so his housemates could sign a new tenancy.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He acknowledges the situation would have been more difficult for his housemates if there wasn't someone who could take his room.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, Eddie thinks the benefits for students are worth this risk.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "If you were to fall out with your flatmates or if you decide that university is not for you, being locked into a full-term contract can be really prohibitive financially," he says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "So without that flexibility, people can really be locked into situations that they don't necessarily want to be in." Lewis Wilson, vice president for higher education at the National Union of Students, says this flexibility means students can also save money on rent by moving home for the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While previously, many student rental contracts ran into the summer after courses had finished, students can now choose to move out earlier if they want.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Wilson says students also benefit from wider changes in the act, which bans landlords in England from evicting tenants without a reason.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Campaigners argue this gives renters greater security and confidence to ask for repairs, without fearing they could be evicted if they raise concerns.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Lewis Wilson from the NUS says the legislation has given students more freedom to move out when they want However, greater flexibility for students to leave tenancies also means less certainty for landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The act did introduce a specific ground , external for landlords to evict a group of students at the end of the academic year if they intend to re-let the property to students.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Chris Norris, chief policy officer at the National Residential Landlords Association, says the bigger problem for student landlords is if their tenants choose to move out earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He argues this is a bigger risk for students - who may fall out with their housemates or drop out of university - than, for example, families, who are less likely to want to move out after just a few months.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says the end of fixed-term tenancies means student houses could be left empty over the summer after courses finish - or even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: He adds that it is now more difficult for student landlords to rent a house for just a few months as they don't know how long the tenants will stay and can't guarantee it will be available for students again in the autumn.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Norris says it's early days for the new legislation and many landlords are taking this year as a test to see how these issues play out in practice.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, he warns that some may choose to increase the monthly rent they charge to cover the risk of their properties being empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: In some cases, he says landlords may even sell up or stop renting to students, reducing supply and pushing up prices.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue Lawes thinks the changes mean many student landlords will put up their rent Sue Lawes, who rents three shared houses to students in Norwich, is worried about the changes.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: While Sue says she doesn't want to put up her prices, if her houses end up being empty over the summer because students decide to end their tenancy after their final exams she says she may have to.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She has already brought forward the start of her tenancy agreements to August instead of September to try and reduce the risks of this.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: However, she says if her tenants move out earlier in the year she would struggle to make a profit, whilst covering costs including her mortgage, council tax and utility standing charges when the properties are empty.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: She argues higher monthly rents would mean bigger upfront costs for students and higher overall costs for those who do choose to carry on renting over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Sue stresses that she supports the aim of the legislation to give tenants greater security and that students should be able to move out if their landlord is not carrying out repairs.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But she wants landlords to be allowed to offer fixed-term contracts to students in line with the academic year to avoid properties being left empty over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords are going to find it very, very hard to absorb those void periods," she says.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: "Landlords will put prices up and students are going to pay." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: At Harrow's Bengaluru campus, students wear the traditional Harrow hats and uniforms On the outskirts of Chandigarh city in India's north-western Punjab state, a 473-year-old legacy British public school opened its first all-girls international campus earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: In contrast to the prominent Gothic-style central building on the school grounds in Bedfordshire, England, the Indian premises are more modern, with purpose-built academic blocks.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But a conspicuous red-brick clock tower bears the imprint of the school's British heritage.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: The Bedford School, Mohali, is the newest in at least half a dozen British public schools (elite, fee-paying private schools with a long history), including three of the country's oldest, that have set up shop across the length and breadth of India.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Their expansion comes amid tighter market conditions in China and the introduction of VAT on private school fees in Britain from 1 January 2025.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Since 2023, Bengaluru - India's Silicon Valley and a hub of software and start-up companies - has been home to the prestigious Harrow School, alma mater of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Queen Elizabeth's School launched in Gurugram near the capital Delhi this August.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Shrewsbury School has a campus in Bhopal in central India, while Wellington College has chosen to set up base in Pune, a western city that calls itself the "Oxford of the East" for its well-regarded universities and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Millfield and a few others are reportedly on their way with satellite campuses in the coming years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: For decades, India has been home to well-established local boarding schools modelled on the colonial British public-school system, serving elite, aristocratic families.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But this market has rapidly expanded with newly wealthy Indian families increasingly aspiring to give their children more global exposure.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "Our international curriculum is quite a driver for many of them," Caroline Pascoe, head of school at Harrow in Bengaluru, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Harrow and Bedford are among the few schools in India that follow an all-through Cambridge curriculum - a global education framework recognised at 10,000 schools worldwide - from primary through to A-levels.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: He said he was also drawn to the fact the school did not have a "VIP culture" unlike many Indian equivalents.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "All kids are treated the same.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Children of ministers and bureaucrats don't get greater privileges," said Singh.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Beyond the growing ranks of well-heeled local families, non-resident Indians who have either returned home after long stints abroad, or those still in the UK or Middle East wanting their children to connect to their roots, are also a significant market for these schools, says Pascoe.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There is also a house system - a hallmark of traditional British education.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: These quintessentially parochial quirks are blended with local customs such as singing the Indian national anthem every morning or celebrating Ganesh Chaturthi, a major Hindu festival.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Schools such as Harrow in Bengaluru promote extracurricular activities like music and drama While India's growing economic credentials and burgeoning population of newly minted millionaires are a natural tailwind for expansion, this growth is partly being driven by a slowdown in China.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Much of the expansion of British public schools abroad in the past decade was driven by China and Hong Kong - half of the 151 satellite campuses operated by 50 UK schools are situated in these countries.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But that growth has slowed following changes in regulation, and "increased scrutiny, and even resistance, from national governments", according to a 2025 study by the UK-based Private Education Policy Forum ( PEPF , external ) think tank.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: A new 2024 Chinese law that required schools to integrate patriotic education into all subjects further challenged expansion and even led to planned campuses being cancelled, prompting these schools to consider other locations like India and Vietnam, according to PEPF.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Moreover, in the 2024 Autumn Budget, Britain introduced a 20% VAT on private school fees.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Naomi Atkins, founding principal at Bedford School Mohali, says this has forced many private schools to look overseas.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "They are in a desperate situation.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even those that hadn't previously looked for international expansion are now suddenly active in India," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Well-heeled local families and non-resident Indians are a major target market for British schools in India But India has not been an easy market, she admits.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Most of these schools are set up in partnership with local investors or operators.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: While in the past schools in other countries might have been able to do deals at 10% of revenue - the fee that they would charge the local partner-investor - margins in India may have shrunk to as low as 1% in some cases, says Atikins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: There has also been some over-estimation of the size of the market, she says.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Even though India has nearly 250 million children enrolled in schools, English education is deeply entrenched in the country and competition from local players is much more intense compared with other non-English speaking countries like China, Korea or Vietnam.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: India's per capita income is also far lower and the high price-points of the British schools - which can charge up to £15,000 or more for full boarding - can limit growth.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: "I've worked in Indonesia, Malaysia and China but Indians are much more price-sensitive - they like a bargain," says Atkins.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: That is why Bedford Mohali has set its fees at roughly half those charged by other British schools.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: Between 2011-12 and 2022-23, the satellite campuses of British schools generated £152.4m in profit, according to PEPF, and this profit has grown substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: But in India, it appears growth is likely to be slow and steady rather than explosive.
sentences.article_title: Britain's posh schools are heading to India for students and profits

sentences.text: The country's old colonial roots and new money afford the legacy institutions a significant business opportunity, but it is unlikely to be big enough to offset the loss of the Chinese market, at least immediately.
